idiom_name: `#[cfg(test)]` helper functions plus `Default` and struct update syntax
implementation_notes: Rust's local idiom is the Default trait plus struct update syntax - Customer { name: "Ada".into(), ..Default::default() } - which gives each test a readable baseline without any mother type, kept out of the shipped crate by #[cfg(test)]. Shared canned fixtures for integration tests live in tests/common/mod.rs (a submodule, so Cargo does not compile it as its own test crate) or in a dedicated test-support crate; derive_builder/typed-builder and the fake crate take over when variation or randomized data grows. A CustomerMother struct with associated functions is justified only when validity depends on cross-field invariants that Default cannot express.
pitfalls: ..Default::default() silently supplies semantically empty values (zero id, empty strings): a fixture can be type-valid and domain-invalid, so Default must be implemented with real invariants or the helper must set every required field.
Files under tests/ are compiled as separate crates; a helper placed at tests/common.rs shows up as an empty test binary, so it must go into tests/common/mod.rs.
Default constructs fresh allocations per call, which is fine for tests, but a static fixture (static/lazy_static/OnceLock) reintroduces shared mutable state and needs interior mutability or a lock.
A helper returning a struct that contains &'static str versus String shapes the whole test suite's lifetime story; mixing them pushes awkward .into() calls into every test.
